summary: Ringu Tulku works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University under Dilgo Khyentse, the 16th Karmapa, and Tubten Tsondru, and founded Bodhicharya.
Rinzin Thargyal is a scholar of Tibetology who completed a Magister degree at the University of Oslo by 1985 under the supervision of Fredrik Barth and temporary supervision of Arne Martin Klausen.

Rita Langer specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, SOAS, and the University of Hamburg (PhD 2004) under Lambert Schmithausen, holding a post at the University of Bristol in 2009.

Rita M. Gross was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. Educated at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee and the University of Chicago, she served as Professor Emerita at the University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire (~1979-1998) and taught at Mindrolling Lotus Garden (~2003-2015).

Rizong Sras Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Monastically trained at Drepung Loseling Monastery (1950-1959) under teachers including Tenzin Gyatso, he served as Abbot of Gyume Tantric Monastery (~1979-1984), Drepung Loseling (1984), and Samstanling Monastery.

Rob Linrothe specializes in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago and held academic posts at Skidmore College (1992-2009) and Northwestern University (2010-2022).

Rob Nairn was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at King's College London, the University of London, Edinburgh, and Zimbabwe. He served as a senior lecturer at the University of Zimbabwe and as a professor of law and criminology at Cape Town.

Robert A. F. Thurman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. After completing his degrees at Harvard University (~1958-1972), he served on the faculty at Amherst College (1973-1988) and as a director at Columbia University (1988-2019).
Robert Alan Goodding is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Texas at Austin in 2002 under the supervision of Patrick Olivelle.

Robert Alexander Neil was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the University of Aberdeen and Peterhouse, Cambridge, he served as University Lecturer in Sanskrit at Cambridge from 1884 and became a Fellow of Pembroke College in 1900.

Robert Anthony Orsi is a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at Trinity College and Yale University. His career includes posts at Fordham, Indiana University, Harvard (2001-2007), and an endowed chair at Northwestern University from around 2007.

Robert B. Ekvall was a Tibetologist who served as a research associate at the University of Chicago (~1953), a research fellow and chairman at the University of Washington (1958), and honorary curator at the Burke Museum (attested 1983).

Robert Baker Aitken was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and Ryutaku-ji under teachers including Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki and Yamada Koun, working at the East-West Center and the University of Hawaiʻi until 1969.

Robert Barnett is a Tibetologist educated at the University of Cambridge. He served at Columbia University (~1999-2018), directed a summer program at Tibet University (2000-2006), and became a Professorial Research Associate at SOAS in 2018.

Robert Buswell is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his AB, MA, and PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (~1979-1985). He served as a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles from ~1993 to 2022.

Robert Caesar Childers was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who studied at Wadham College, Oxford. He served as a sub-librarian at the India Office (1872) and professor of Pali at University College London (~1872-1876).

Robert Chalmers was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oriel College, Oxford, under T. W. Rhys Davids. He served as president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1922-1925) and Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge (1924-1931).

Robert Chambers was an Indologist educated at Lincoln College, Oxford. He served as Vinerian Professor of English Law at Oxford (1766), Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William (~1791-1798), and president of The Asiatic Society (~1797-1799).

Robert Charles Zaehner was a scholar of religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. Educated at Christ Church, Oxford, and Cambridge, he held posts at Oxford as Lecturer in Persian (1950) and Professor of Eastern Religions (1952).

Robert DeCaroli is a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his MA and PhD at UCLA under Katherine Anne Harper and Robert L. Brown, and joined the faculty of George Mason University around 1999.
